object_description: four longitudinal structures staggered parallel to the slope edge, tied into one wooden framework
geometry_property: staggered parallel to the slope edge
one two-storey head, three single-storey wings
design_condition: the four wings step parallel to the edge of the slope, forming a clear edge with covered outdoor space towards the path and defining a protected sunny outdoor space towards the ravine with an L-shaped figure

positive: The programme is divided into four longitudinal structures tied together in one large wooden framework
A clear edge with covered outdoor space is created as address and entrance
An L-shaped basic figure defines a protected, well-sunny outdoor space towards the ravine
The taller middle building overlooks the others and houses the day care while the wings stay single-storey
The complex enters into a dialogue with the existing school building and the church across the ravine
The front building defines a credible conclusion and connects the area to the sports field
The lower part of the property remains undeveloped as a long-term reserve
The kindergarten roofs are accessible from the day care and serve as self-contained, easily visible outdoor space
South-facing skylights allow views back into the kindergarten rooms from the roofs
A covered corridor leads from the narrow entrance area into the depth of the property
The kitchen at the entrance corner overlooks the entrance situations and gathers the children at lunchtime
Two pragmatically designed staircases continue the movement of the facility inside and zone the volume
They end in a gallery from which one looks down to the roofs and into the distance
Flexible, simply placed walls allow separation of zones or use as one large connected room
The kindergarten units are cleverly zoned by a deep shelf usable from both sides
Mobile walls create beautifully proportioned divisions and open room situations
The facade language is simple but elegantly proportioned and develops from the wooden framework
The facility complements and interprets the location very independently, conserves resources and is spatially generous
Superimposing the gridded structure with staged visual connections develops a specific design logic
It translates the potential of location and programme into architecture without applying artificial images
The limit distances are adhered to
The building frames a spacious, slightly terraced garden space that expands towards the street
The volume and the grove create a quiet courtyard for playing and spending time outdoors
The roof areas of the single-storey wings are offered as play and lounge areas
negative: The distance to the forest is not reached
The summer linden tree worth preserving cannot be preserved
The line-up of equipment in the kindergarten area seems disturbing and somewhat helpless
